memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: So Joshua ordered the officers of the people: "Go through the camp and tell the people, 'Get your provisions ready. Three days from now you will cross the Jordan here to go in and take possession of the land the Lord your God is giving you for your own.'" — Josh 1:10-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God had spoken; now Joshua acts. Notice how quickly obedience follows the promise. Joshua does not call a committee or wait for a sign. He hears God, and he moves the people forward. Faith that truly believes God's promise gets up and prepares.

There is a beautiful balance here. God said, "the land I am about to give you." It is a gift. Yet Joshua tells the people, "Get your provisions ready." They still had to prepare, pack, and walk. God's gift and our responsibility are not enemies. We do not earn what God freely gives, but we do respond to it with action. Grace is never an excuse for laziness.

The "three days" gave the people time to prepare their hearts as well as their supplies. Sometimes God gives us a short season to get ready for a big step. Those in-between days are not wasted; they are part of the journey.

The whole land was a gift of grace, pointing forward to the greater inheritance we receive freely in Christ (Eph 2:8-9). And just as Israel prepared to cross into their inheritance, we live ready, walking forward in the good works God has prepared for us.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When God speaks to you, do you move promptly, or delay?
2. Are you treating God's grace as a reason to sit still, or to step out?
3. Is God giving you an "in-between" season right now to prepare for something ahead?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me respond to Your promises with ready obedience. Teach me to prepare well and to move when You say move. Amen.
